pricing.rule: Each delivered call bills price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005. A pending/async ack or an unverifiable charged call (delivered:false, refundable:false) bills price_usd × 1.15 with no per-call fee; refunded calls, in-batch duplicates and failed runs bill $0. A call runs only when its full delivered amount fits the batch's remaining max_usd, so max_usd must be at least Σ(price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005).

🚨 SI Narrative Alert Federal Reserve officially adopts SI

31 October 2026 briefing | Narrative significance: HIGH

Two meaningful developments have emerged since the previous briefing: the Federal Reserve has officially updated its terminology to Super Intelligence (SI), and CNBC has published new coverage examining adoption of the terminology across major technology companies.

1. Federal Reserve confirms AI-to-SI terminology change
Federal Reserve Board
Official website updated 30 October 2026
The Federal Reserve Board has published an official page titled Super Intelligence (SI) Program.
It explicitly confirms that references to artificial intelligence were updated to super intelligence where appropriate, following President Trump's September executive order.

The page also identifies Anderson Monken as Chief Super Intelligence Officer (CSIO).

The programme covers responsible internal use, innovation, governance and risk management. ￼
Why this matters: This is another concrete institutional implementation of the terminology change, rather than a politician simply mentioning SI.

It also brings the abbreviation into the public-facing communications of one of the world's most influential financial institutions.

However, this is an administrative terminology update, not a new monetary-policy decision, technology breakthrough or financial investment.

2. CNBC highlights a split among major technology CEOs
New mainstream-media coverage — 30 October
CNBC published an article examining how leading technology executives are responding to Trump's SI terminology campaign.

Its findings are particularly interesting:

Elon Musk Used SI on Tesla's earnings call

Mark Zuckerberg Promoted personal superintelligence

Satya Nadella Used AI publicly, but Microsoft's shareholder letter also embraces Super Intelligence

Arvind Krishna, IBM Used both AI and super intelligence

Lip-Bu Tan, Intel Referred to demand for super intelligence

Sundar Pichai, Alphabet Continued using AI
Andy Jassy, Amazon Continued using AI

The underlying executive statements are mostly from earlier earnings calls. What's new is CNBC's comparative reporting and the additional mainstream exposure it gives the terminology debate. 

The strongest new signal is the Federal Reserve's explicit confirmation that it has updated its terminology.
Combined with the previously reported US–Finland agreement, this provides further evidence that SI is moving beyond presidential rhetoric into institutional and international documentation.
